message.content: The Los Angeles Lakers won the NBA Finals in the 2019-2020 season, defeating the Miami Heat 4-2 [1][2][3][5][6]. This victory marked their 17th championship title in franchise history [4]. LeBron James was named Finals MVP for the fourth time in his career, averaging 29.8 points, 11.8 rebounds, and 8.5 assists per game [1][3]. The series concluded in October 2020 inside the NBA's "bubble" at Walt Disney World due to the COVID-19 pandemic [2].

passages.heading: 2020 NBA Finals
passages.text: The **2020 NBA Finals** was the championship series of the National Basketball Association's (NBA) 2019–20 season and conclusion of the season's playoffs. In this best-of-seven playoff series, the Western Conference champion Los Angeles Lakers defeated the Eastern Conference champion Miami Heat, 4–2 and 17th title overall in franchise history. The Los Angeles Lakers also became the first and only team in NBA history to be undefeated in a season when leading entering the fourth quarter, going a combined 57–0 record in the regular season and playoffs. The Lakers' LeBron James was named the NBA Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP) for the fourth time in his career. He became the first and only player in NBA history to be named Finals MVP with three different franchises (two with the Heat, one with the Cleveland Cavaliers, and one with the Lakers) and along with teammate Danny Green, jointly the third players to win the NBA Finals with three different teams. He won the Finals MVP award in a unanimous 11–0 vote by leading his team in points, rebounds, and assists for the entire series, after averaging 29.8 points, 11.8 rebounds, and 8.5 assists per game on the very efficient 59% shooting. Lakers president Jeanie Buss became the first female controlling owner to guide her team to an NBA title.

passages.heading: Los Angeles Lakers
passages.text: The Lakers clinched their first playoff berth since the 2012–13 season in March 2020, days before the season was suspended.<sup>[19]</sup><sup>[20]</sup> It ended the longest drought in the franchise's history.<sup>[20]</sup> After play resumed in the bubble, the Lakers clinched both their first Pacific Division title since 2012 and the top seed in the Western Conference playoffs for the first time since the 2009–10 season.<sup>[21]</sup> James and Davis were runner-ups for the NBA Most Valuable Player and NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award, respectively, behind Giannis Antetokounmpo, and both were named to the All-NBA First Team.<sup>[22]</sup>

passages.heading: Aftermath
passages.text: The following 2020–21 season began on December 22, 72 days after the Lakers won the championship. The extremely short offseason proved detrimental for both the Heat and the Lakers. Los Angeles finished the 72-game schedule at 42–30, seventh in the Western Conference, while Miami went 40–32 to finish sixth in the Eastern Conference. Injuries to LeBron James and Anthony Davis, among others, derailed the Lakers' season. After defeating the Golden State Warriors in the play-in tournament and qualified for the 2021 NBA playoffs, the Lakers lost in the first round to the Phoenix Suns 4–2. It marked the first time LeBron James failed to win a single playoff series in a season.<sup>[68]</sup> Meanwhile, the Heat were swept by the eventual champion Milwaukee Bucks in the first round.

sources.title: Lakers news: LeBron James still wishes LA had 2020 championship parade

passages.text:
*Lakers news: LeBron James still wishes LA had 2020 championship parade* *appeared first on* *ClutchPoints**. Add ClutchPoints as a* *Preferred Source by clicking here**.*

In the 23 NBA seasons that he has played so far, LeBron James has won four championships. While he is now with the Philadelphia 76ers after signing a two-year, $8 million contract, there is one part of his 2020 title run with the Los Angeles Lakers that he still wishes he could have experienced.

The Lakers never got to celebrate their championship with a traditional parade because of COVID-19 restrictions. Six years later, James still thinks about what that celebration could have looked like.

"That bothers me 1 to 10. 20 like just to be able to celebrate with the Laker faithful," he recently said on Mind the Game podcast. "I don't know what the route would have been. I'm thinking go down Olympic just like all the way down Olympic and then end up downtown right by Staple Center. They want to call it Crypto and sh*t, I call it Staple Center to me. It would have been super duper dope, man. But yeah, we did that. We did that. And that banner is up there. That banner is in that arena forever along with the other ones that been able to go up in the history of the Lakers Franchise."

*Watch sports LIVE with* *fuboTV (free trial)*

The 2019-20 Lakers won the championship inside the NBA's Orlando bubble after the league suspended the season for several months during the pandemic. The team eventually returned to action in a closed environment at Walt Disney World, where the Lakers beat the Miami Heat in the NBA Finals.

The title also came during a difficult year for the Lakers organization following the death of Kobe Bryant in January 2020.

James has often pointed to the unique challenges of that postseason when discussing the championship. Players spent months away from their families and played without fans in the arena.

The Lakers did eventually raise the 2020 championship banner at Crypto.com Arena.

passages.text:
# NBA Champions by Year: Complete list of NBA Finals winners

The __NBA__ Finals are chock-full of history and iconic moments. We've seen legendary franchises, like the Boston Celtics and Los Angeles Lakers, dominate the league, as well as newer powerhouses like the Golden State Warriors and Miami Heat. This year, Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks defeated Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs for their first title in 53 years.

Let's take a look back at the complete list of NBA Finals winners.

passages.heading: **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have won the most NBA championships?**

The Celtics have the most NBA titles with 18. Here’s a list of teams that have won at least three NBA championships:

- Boston Celtics (18 titles)
- Los Angeles Lakers (17)
- Golden State Warriors (7)
- Chicago Bulls (6)
- San Antonio Spurs (5)
- Philadelphia 76ers (3)
- Detroit Pistons (3)
- Miami Heat (3)

passages.heading: **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**
passages.text:
### **Which teams have never won an NBA championship?**

Ten NBA franchises have never won an NBA Finals:

- Brooklyn Nets
- Charlotte Hornets
- Indiana Pacers
- Los Angeles Clippers
- Memphis Grizzlies
- Minnesota Timberwolves
- New Orleans Pelicans
- Orlando Magic
- Phoenix Suns
- Utah Jazz
